notes: Single source of truth for the lead engine's MongoDB collections. Applied by services/src/db/migrate.js (production) and by ingest/src/leadengine/schema.py (tests and local set-up). Validators run on every insert and update, so the rules below are enforced by the database itself, not only by our code.

companies.purpose: One record per company, keyed on its CIN or LLPIN. Uttar Pradesh only.

state.description: The engine covers Uttar Pradesh only; any other state is refused.

people.purpose: Directors and contacts. Every contact point carries its source, legal basis and verification; consent itself is recorded in consents.

source_records.purpose: Raw records exactly as each source gave them. Never edited: a changed record is stored as a new version with a new content hash.

ingest_runs.purpose: One document per collector, knowledge-base or nightly run: what was fetched, what changed, what failed. At most one nightly run is 'running' at a time (the one_running_nightly index is its lock).

leads.purpose: A company we may contact, with its current stage. One lead per company. Rebuilt nightly by the need engine; the stage only moves forward, and the holdout draw never changes once made.

holdout.description: True for the random 10% that is never contacted.

holdout_draw.description: How the holdout decision was made: a keyed hash of the company id, so it is random, stable and reproducible.

rules_confirmed.description: False until a CA has signed off the rules; unconfirmed needs are never used in a message.

activities.purpose: Every touch and outcome, append-only. The single source for the dashboard and attribution.

consents.purpose: Consent ledger. Append-only and hash-chained: each entry carries the hash of the one before it, so any later edit or deletion is detectable.

suppressions.purpose: One do-not-contact list for every channel. Keyed on an HMAC of the normalised address under CONTACT_KEY_SECRET (kept outside the database); erasure requests keep only the key. The application can add and update entries but never delete one.

erased_at.description: When an erasure request blanked this entry's address and note.

source_state.purpose: Which version of each source record is current, and when it was last seen. source_records keeps every version ever seen; this points at the current one, so a record that changes back to an earlier version is still read correctly.

entity_links.purpose: The knowledge base's answer to 'which company is this?' for every entity that has no CIN of its own (today, a startup known only by its UPLC number). Rebuilt by the nightly matching run; a person's decision in match_reviews always wins.

matcher.description: the matcher's own decision before any reviewer's (status, company_id, method, probability); precision is measured on it

ai_check.description: the AI model's advice on an unsure pair (services/src/admin/ai_check.js): never a decision

match_reviews.purpose: A person's (or, later, the AI checker's) decision on one candidate pair. These override the matcher and double as the labelled set that measures matching precision.

enrichment_cache.purpose: Every enrichment answer, found or not found, with its expiry (company facts 90 days, contact details 30). A cached 'not found' stops us paying twice for nothing. MongoDB deletes expired entries itself.

usage.purpose: Counters behind the hard caps in config/caps.json (paid lookups a month, free lookups a day, ...) and each mailbox's sends per IST day. A unit is taken atomically before the call or the send, so two workers cannot overrun a cap between them.

audit_log.purpose: Every view or export of personal data in the Admin pages, every review decision, every sign-in (accepted or refused) and sign-out, every import of match labels, every erasure, every decision on a reply, and every platform event that was refused, every MCA file uploaded, every bulk export asked for and decided; append-only (design 7.11).

revoked_sessions.purpose: Admin sign-in sessions ended by signing out, keyed on a hash of the session's signature. A session cookie lives at most 12 hours, so each entry is deleted by the TTL index when the session would have expired anyway.

_id.description: sha256 of the session cookie's signature

llm_calls.purpose: Every AI call with its model, tokens and cost, so the AI cost per lead is always known.

jobs.purpose: The schedule of every pending step. Workers claim due jobs atomically; the idempotency key stops a retry from repeating a side effect.

deferrals.description: How often the step was told to wait (send window, daily cap); waiting never uses up an attempt.

cancel_requested.description: cancel() arrived while an attempt was running: the job is cancelled instead of retried.

messages.purpose: Every outreach message from draft to outcome (design 7.5): the evidence pack it was written from, the draft, the quality check, the person's approval (with a hash of exactly what they approved), the compliance gate's answer and the send. One per company, kind and need (idem_key). A working collection: an erasure request blanks the recipient's address here.

need_id.description: For a new-need message, the need it is about: d:<deadline>:<date> or s:<scheme>.

page_tokens.purpose: The unguessable links: a company's page and its unsubscribe link (in a message), and the link that confirms a claim made from a campaign page. Only a SHA-256 of each token is stored, so a copy of the database cannot be used to open a page or unsubscribe someone. Expired tokens are removed by the TTL index.

campaign.description: campaign:<code> for a link opened from a campaign landing page

pending.description: claim_confirm only: the claim from a campaign page waiting for its email confirmation (the form as given, with the consent wording shown). It leaves with the token: used once, or removed by the TTL index after 48 hours.

channel_templates.purpose: What Meta says about each WhatsApp template (status, category, quality rating), read by `lead-engine whatsapp:templates --sync` and kept current by Meta's webhook. A template is sent only while it is APPROVED here, so a template Meta pauses stops at once (design 7.6).

reason.description: Meta's reason, when its webhook paused, disabled or rejected the template.

inbound.purpose: Every email that arrived in an outreach mailbox, and every WhatsApp message a founder sent to our number (design 7.5 and 7.6). Emails are read with IMAP EXAMINE, so the mailbox itself is never changed. Each one is matched to the message it answers, classified (reply, auto-reply, bounce, complaint; a reply as interested, not now, unsubscribe, wrong person or question), and acted on: a bounce suppresses the address, an opt-out suppresses it and stops the sequence, and everything a person must answer waits in the Admin inbox. A working collection holding personal data (the sender's address and words): removed by the TTL index after the retention period, and blanked by an erasure request.

idem_key.description: in:<mailbox>:<uidvalidity>:<uid> for an email, in:whatsapp:<message id> for WhatsApp

channel.description: Missing means email (everything read before WhatsApp replies were kept here).

dsn.description: The delivery report of a bounce: recipient, action, status code, diagnostic.

text.description: The new part of the reply (quoted text removed), at most a few thousand characters.

status.description: new while the engine is still acting on it; needs_person until someone has dealt with it; done when the engine dealt with it alone; ignored when it is not about our outreach (warm-up mail, newsletters).

actions.description: What the engine did on reading it.

calls.purpose: Every AI voice call (design 7.6): only to a founder who asked for a call on the company page, through the voice provider on a DLT-registered number, inside the permitted hours and the month's caps, with an approved script that says at once that it is an AI assistant. One document per attempt, from queued to its outcome. Holds the number called and the transcript, so it is a working collection: removed by the TTL index after the retention period and blanked by an erasure request.

handled.description: A person dealt with it (made the call, or followed up the outcome): by, at, note.

alerts.purpose: What `lead-engine monitor` found wrong (design 7.10): failed and overdue jobs, bounce and complaint rates, WhatsApp template quality, approval-queue and inbox age, caps nearly used, a stale nightly run, a consent ledger that does not verify. One document per alert key; it is reopened when the problem comes back and resolved when it goes.

locks.purpose: Short-lived holds that make check-then-act steps safe across workers: 'lead:<company_id>' while a message to that company is being sent (contact budget), and 'ledger:consents', which every consent-ledger transaction updates so that entries are added one at a time. The application can add and update these but never delete one.

email_checks.purpose: The result of checking an address before the first email to it (design 7.3): well formed, not a throwaway domain, the domain receives mail, and the verification service's verdict. Keyed on an HMAC of the address under CONTACT_KEY_SECRET, never the address; each entry expires (30 days, or a day when the check could not be done).

exports.purpose: Bulk exports of company-level data (design 7.11): asked for with a reason, approved or rejected by an admin who is not the person asking, then downloadable by the person who asked for 24 hours. Kept as the record of who took what out of the engine; never deleted.

signals.purpose: Funding news about a UP company (design 7.1 and 7.4, 'Signals'), from news feeds and GDELT (`leadengine ingest news`): a headline whose company name matched exactly one company. Only a proposal until a reviewer confirms or rejects it on the Admin Signals page (the decision is in audit_log); nothing acts on a signal by itself. Holds the headline, link, publisher and date only, never an article's text; news that matched no company is not stored. Keyed on a hash of the article's URL, so reading the same article again changes nothing.
